messages.subject: covariance estimates for observed variables with lavaan
parts:
Dear all,
I am puzzled with the behavior of R's ```lavaan``` package. I am trying to estimate the variances and covariances of two observed variables. 

Here is the data:

```
bd <- data.frame(
          Group = c(1L,1L,1L,1L,1L,1L,1L,1L,1L,1L,1L,
                 3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,3L,2L,
                 2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,2L,
                 2L),
          HIP_D = c(2763,3241.5,2740.5,3318,3501,3634.5,
                 4324.5,2970,3168,3307.5,3145.5,3639,3325.5,3295.5,3066,
                 3711,2488.5,3333,3138,2752.5,3096,2785.5,3204,3781.5,
                 3207,2742,3082.5,2665.5,2737.5,2664,2743.5,2695.5,3244.5,
                 3024,2422.5,1605,2943,2314.5,2971.5,3187,2673,3024,
                 2992.5),
          HIP_E = c(2505,3292.5,2646.7,3457.5,3505.5,
                 3628.5,4152,2686.5,2943,2913,3283.5,3546,3172.5,3090,3211.5,
                 3880.5,1725,3147,3055.5,2776.5,2904,2785.5,3159,
                 3418.5,3240,2334,2634,2370,2736,2503.5,2325,2409,3057,
                 2692.5,2443.5,1645.5,2922,1818,2679,2742,2465.5,2911.5,
                 2890.5)
)
```

My code is as follows:

```
modVL <- '
HIP_D ~~ HIP_D
HIP_E ~~ HIP_E
HIP_D ~~ HIP_E
'
library(lavaan)
fitVL <- sem(modVL, data=bd, likelihood = "wishart",  orthogonal = FALSE)
summary(fitVL, standardize=T)
```
And the output is:
```
lavaan 0.6-7 ended normally after 8 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML
  Optimization method                           NLMINB
  Number of free parameters                          3
                                                      
  Number of observations                            43
                                                      
Model Test User Model:
                                                      
  Test statistic                                81.564
  Degrees of freedom                                 0

Parameter Estimates:

  Standard errors                             Standard
  Information                                 Expected
  Information saturated (h1) model          Structured

Covariances:
                   Estimate    Std.Err   z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv    Std.all
  HIP_D ~~                                                                   
    HIP_E               0.000 36570.317    0.000    1.000      0.000    0.000

Variances:
                   Estimate    Std.Err   z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv    Std.all
    HIP_D          203990.618 44514.402    4.583    0.000 203990.618    1.000
    HIP_E          275357.264 60087.881    4.583    0.000 275357.264    1.000
```

Now, the two variables (HIP_D and HIP_E) are very strongly correlated:
```
correlation::correlation(bd)

Parameter1 | Parameter2 |    r |       95% CI |     t | df |      p |  Method | n_Obs
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
HIP_D      |      HIP_E | 0.93 | [0.87, 0.96] | 15.65 | 41 | < .001 | Pearson |    43
```
So, there's no way the covariance could be zero!... I am puzzled with how lavaan is forcing the covariance to zero?

Any thoughts?

Thanks!

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: covariance estimates for observed variables with lavaan
parts: Notice also the positive chi-square value, despite the model being saturated, with DF = 0. If you request fit indices, you will see that the reported chi-square for your target model is the same as the reported chi-square for the null model. So the zero covariance here is the covariance value for the null model. The question is, why is lavaan reporting fit and parameter estimates for the null model instead of the target model?

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: covariance estimates for observed variables with lavaan
parts:
Not a bug per se, but an issue with scaling. With the large variances for HIP_D and HIP_E the estimator is ending up in some odd places. If you rescale the variables by dividing each one by 100 you can reproduce the correlation:

bd$HIP_D2 <- bd$HIP_D/100
bd$HIP_E2 <- bd$HIP_E/100

modVL <- '
HIP_D2 ~~ HIP_D2
HIP_E2 ~~ HIP_E2
HIP_D2 ~~ HIP_E2
'

fitVL <- sem(modVL, data=bd, likelihood = "wishart",  orthogonal = FALSE)
summary(fitVL, standardize=T)

Notice also the positive chi-square value, despite the model being saturated, with DF = 0. messages.subject: Re: covariance estimates for observed variables with lavaan
parts: I'm sure Yves could weigh in with more detail, I'll say from my experience if your estimates of variances are >10,000 that's the point where things get odd. Also, the issue isn't simply the size of the variances, but also the differences in scaling (e.g. if you have two variables with variances of .01 and 100 that can be an issue too, though in that case lavaan gives you a warning). One other note: this is not a lavaan specific issue, it's an issue for maximum likelihood.

A quinta-feira, 15 de outubro de 2020 à(s) 18:35:51 UTC+1, alexander...@gmail.com escreveu:
Not a bug per se, but an issue with scaling. With the large variances for HIP_D and HIP_E the estimator is ending up in some odd places. If you rescale the variables by dividing each one by 100 you can reproduce the correlation:

bd$HIP_D2 <- bd$HIP_D/100
bd$HIP_E2 <- bd$HIP_E/100

modVL <- '
HIP_D2 ~~ HIP_D2
HIP_E2 ~~ HIP_E2
HIP_D2 ~~ HIP_E2
'
fitVL <- sem(modVL, data=bd, likelihood = "wishart",  orthogonal = FALSE)
summary(fitVL, standardize=T)
